title: Pretrained Models in torchvision 🏋️
description: Load powerful models like ResNet and EfficientNet with pretrained weights.

slides.title: The Model Zoo 🦁
slides.content:
# torchvision.models

PyTorch provides many pretrained architectures ready to use:
* **ResNet** (18, 34, 50, 101, 152)
* **EfficientNet** (B0–B7)
* **VGG**, **DenseNet**, **MobileNet**, **ConvNeXt**, etc.

All come with `weights` parameter to load pretrained weights.

slides.title: Loading a Pretrained ResNet
slides.codeSnippet:
import torchvision.models as models

# New API (recommended)
model = models.resnet18(weights=models.ResNet18_Weights.DEFAULT)
print(model)
# Look at the final fully‑connected layer (fc)

quizData.question: Which argument loads ImageNet pretrained weights into ResNet18?
quizData.explanation: The new API uses the `weights` parameter with an enum. `pretrained=True` is deprecated.

slides.title: Inspecting the Architecture 🔍
slides.content:
## Finding the Classifier Head

Pretrained models on ImageNet have a final layer with **1000** output classes. To adapt to a new task, we need to replace this layer. 

Common names for the classifier:
* ResNet: `model.fc`
* VGG: `model.classifier[6]`
* EfficientNet: `model.classifier[1]`

We'll replace it with a new `nn.Linear` matching our number of classes.

slides.title: Replacing the Final Layer
slides.codeSnippet:
num_classes = 10
model = models.resnet18(weights=models.ResNet18_Weights.DEFAULT)
# Replace fc layer
in_features = model.fc.in_features
model.fc = nn.Linear(in_features, num_classes)
print(model.fc)

quizData.question: Why do we replace the final layer of a pretrained model?

options.text: To match the output classes of the new task

quizData.explanation: The original output layer predicts 1000 ImageNet classes; we need a layer with our number of classes.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Weights Transform

When loading pretrained weights, you can also access the associated preprocessing transforms: `weights.transforms()` provides the required mean, std, and image size.
